claims.text: Qsymia peds: indicated in adults and peds ≥ 12 y w obesity;
claims.quote: Adults and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with obesity

claims.text: after 12 wk on 7.5/46 mg, peds w BMI ↓ < 3%: 11.25/69 mg × 14 d, then 15/92 mg;
claims.quote: After 12 weeks of treatment with QSYMIA 7.5 mg/46 mg, evaluate weight loss for adults or BMI reduction for pediatric patients aged 12 years and older. If an adult patient has not lost at least 3% of baseline body weight or a pediatric patient has not experienced a reduction of at least 3% of baseline BMI, increase the dosage to QSYMIA 11.25 mg/69 mg orally once daily for 14 days; followed by an increase in the dosage to QSYMIA 15 mg/92 mg orally once daily.

claims.text: stop if BMI ↓ < 5% after 12 wk on 15/92 mg;
claims.quote: After 12 weeks of treatment with QSYMIA 15 mg/92 mg, evaluate weight loss for adults or BMI reduction for pediatric patients aged 12 years and older. If an adult patient has not lost at least 5% of baseline body weight or a pediatric patient has not experienced a reduction of at least 5% of baseline BMI, discontinue QSYMIA

claims.text: wt loss > 2 lbs (0.9 kg)/wk: consider a lower dose;
claims.quote: Monitor the rate of weight loss in pediatric patients. If weight loss exceeds 2 lbs (0.9 kg)/week, consider dosage reduction.

claims.text: slowed linear growth: consider a lower dose or stopping.
claims.quote: Slowing of Linear Growth: Consider dosage reduction or discontinuation if pediatric patients are not growing or gaining height as expected

claims.text: Contrave: not approved for use in pediatric pts.
claims.quote: CONTRAVE is not approved for use in pediatric patients

claims.text: Qsymia: 3.75/23 mg PO each Am × 14 d, then 7.5/46 mg.
claims.quote: The recommended starting dosage of QSYMIA is one capsule (containing 3.75 mg of phentermine and 23 mg of topiramate) (3.75 mg/23 mg) taken orally once daily for 14 days; after 14 days increase to the recommended dosage of QSYMIA 7.5 mg/46 mg orally once daily.

claims.text: Birth-defect risk: give to women of reprod age only w contraception and monthly preg tests.
claims.quote: Because birth defects are a risk, the combination should be given to women of reproductive age only if they are using contraception and are tested monthly for pregnancy.
